messages:
evan-sales: Customer wants a clear POC plan for a warm standby in an air-gapped DR site. Main asks: bundle delivery options, expected delta sizes for monthly patches, and an economical standby pricing model.

rachel-se: Good call. Do they require full model replication on the standby or just runtime + weights on demand? That changes transport.

evans-sales: They asked for full replication so the DR site can take traffic with no network dependency.

josh-eng: Full replication single-shot means we ship a base image + model artifacts. For ongoing patches we can send signed delta archives. Typical delta for small dev models ~100-300MB, for large LLMs with weight-only diffs could be multiple GBs depending on quantization changes.

marta-security: Security checklist: signed manifest, chain-of-trust for artifact signing, offline SBOM, and proof of checksums. They also want the signing cert thumbprint recorded in the SOW.

rachel-se: Transport options to propose: 1) encrypted USB handoff (sneakernet) 2) couriered NVMe with manifests 3) SFTP drop in a DMZ that customer pulls from internal airgap. Need to include sizing + cost assumptions for courier.

josh-eng: Operationally, two packaging profiles: "full replicate" (container + model archive, larger disk) and "compact warm" (runtime + compact prefix cache). Compact warm reduces bundle size by ~60-80% but may increase first-request latency until cache regenerates.

evans-sales: They also asked about monthly validation windows where we run a smoke test on standby. Would that count as run-hours or is it included?

marta-security: From compliance, monthly validation should be auditable. We need signed test manifests and results stored in the install record.

rachel-se: Pricing approach suggestion: base standby seat (lower monthly) + buffered run-hours for DR drills and failovers. Offer an annual commit discount and credits for scheduled DR exercises to reduce surprise costs. Example: $X/month standby fee + $Y/hr above baseline.

josh-eng: Failover latency expectations: if image + model already mounted and prefix cache present, <45s to flip routing and warm containers. If we need to ingest from physical media and extract model weights, plan for 10–40 minutes depending on I/O.

evans-sales: Customer target was <2 minutes ideally. We should be explicit: meet 2 min only with compact hot-cache preloaded and image pre-pulled.

marta-security: HSM/KMS in airgapped site: we support customer-managed HSM appliances. Installer supports key-injection offline via `rwdctl inject-key --hsm /dev/hsm0 --cert signed.pem`. Document key custody steps.

josh-eng: Add runbook snippet: `rwdctl install --bundle ./redwood-full-2026-03.tar.gz --verify ./manifest.sig --inject-key ./hsm-token` and an offline healthcheck `rwdctl healthcheck --mode offline`. Include time estimates for each phase.

ops-bot: Artifact build 2026.03.20-onprem-full completed. minibundle.tar.gz (3.1GB), compact-prefix.tar.gz (750MB), manifest.sig.

evans-sales: Nice. Action items: Josh -> produce example delta sizes for two model families and a table mapping packaging profile to expected failover times. Marta -> draft the security attestation text and key injection steps. Rachel -> vendor courier cost assumptions and pricing sketch. I'll draft SOW language around scheduled DR credits.

josh-eng: Will get drafts by EOD Friday.

marta-security: I have a template for attestations, will tailor and share tomorrow.

rachel-se: I'll mock a courier price table and sample SOW clause, pinging legal for sample retention wording.

evans-sales: Great — i'll schedule a 30m call with customer PM once we have draft artifacts. :rocket:
